title: The Little Prince, Saint-Exupéry
subject: litterature
description: A little prince from a tiny planet teaches the pilot that what is essential is invisible to the eyes.

hero.hook: To tame is to create links: the lesson of the fox has become universal.

blocks.text: **The Little Prince**, published in **1943**, is the most translated French book in the world, with versions in more than **300 languages**. Behind the simplicity of the pencil line lies a meditation on the human condition, otherness and the quest for meaning.

Written in exile during the Second World War, it is the spiritual testament of **Antoine de Saint-Exupéry**, born in **1900** and died in **1944**. Pilot of the , a French mail transport company, he seeks in the innocence of childhood a remedy for the disenchantment of the adult world. [[Aéropostale]]

blocks.caption: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry, writer-pilot who disappeared at sea in 1944.

blocks.text: The **July 31, 1944**, his plane, a , twin-engine reconnaissance, disappeared in the Mediterranean Sea. Its wreck was not identified until 2000, off the coast of Marseille. [[Lockheed P-38 Lightning]]
Saint-Exupéry never experienced the global success of his work. The original manuscript did not show a sheep in a crate: a friend suggested that he hide it to leave room for the reader's imagination.

sections.title: The Journey of the Little Prince: a satire of modernity

blocks.text: The story opens with a breakdown in the middle of the Sahara. The narrator, a pilot in distress, meets a small being from the asteroid **B-612**. We uproot the , giant trees symbolizing the dangers that must be eradicated as soon as they appear, to save our tiny planet. [[baobabs]]

blocks.caption: The original watercolors of Saint-Exupéry: simplicity and depth.

blocks.text: From planet to planet, the Little Prince meets adults obsessed: the **King** by absolute power, the **Conceited** by narcissism, the **Businessman** by the accounting possession of the stars. Only the **Lighter of street lights** finds favor, because he lights the world for others, without seeking to dominate.

sections.title: The fox and the philosophy of taming

blocks.text: On Earth, lost among five thousand roses, the Little Prince thinks his **Pink** is ordinary. The **Fox** teaches him to **tame**: create bonds that make the other unique in the world. “You become forever responsible for what you have tamed. »
We only see clearly with the heart. The essential is invisible to the eyes.
blocks.attribution: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry, The Little Prince

blocks.text: A being's truth lies in relationship, not in appearance. The ending, where the Little Prince accepts the snake's bite to return to his planet, remains one of the most ambiguous in literature. Death, journey or redemption? The question remains open.
The book can be read at all ages: a story for children, criticism of materialism for adults. The asteroid **46610** was named  in homage to the character's space address B-612. [[Bésixdouze]]

The design of the hat which is in reality a boa having eaten an elephant has become the symbol of imagination against narrow rationalism. What has been tamed survives distance and time: the lesson of the fox resonates well beyond the war that saw the birth of the tale.

**The Little Prince**, written in exile before the death of Saint-Exupéry in **1944**, is a universal fable about taming and responsibility, which has become the most widely distributed French work in the world.
